title: Simple Validator
story: Your social app needs username validation. Usernames must be 3-16 characters, no numbers, no special symbols. Instead of returning cryptic error codes ("-4"), you return meaningful enum variants like `TooShort(3)` or `HasSpecial` so the UI can show "Username must be at least 3 characters."
why: Validation enums replace error codes with self-documenting variants that carry useful data.
analogy: Validation is like a bouncer at a club checking IDs. Valid means "come in." TooShort is "sorry, you're too young" (with the minimum age). HasSpecial is "no fake IDs." Each rejection tells you exactly why you can't enter.
try_it: Add a `HasSpace` variant for usernames containing spaces. Add a `StartsWithNumber` variant. Test: validate "hello world", "9lives", "ok", "a_very_long_username_that_exceeds_sixteen". Write the actual length check logic.
tips: Return the first validation error you encounter � don't try to list all problems at once
Include the threshold in the variant data: `TooShort(min: Int)` so the UI can show "must be at least 3"
Use simple string matching to detect patterns: check for digits and special characters manually
common_mistakes: Returning Valid after finding a problem because you used `if` instead of `if/else if` � the last check overwrites earlier failures
Not including the threshold in the variant � without `min`, the caller can't build a precise error message
